title: Verification loop shadowed zsh PATH through special path variable
description: A repository verification command used `path` as a loop variable. In zsh, `path` is a special array tied to `PATH`, so subsequent rg, tail, and shasum commands could not be found.

context.code_snippet: for path in .dockerignore DOCKER.md Dockerfile docker-compose.yml; do ...; done

error_message: zsh:1: command not found: rg; zsh:1: command not found: tail; zsh:1: command not found: shasum
root_cause: The verification command overlooked that `path` is a reserved special parameter in zsh and unintentionally replaced the executable search path.
solution: Renamed the loop variable to `target_file` and reran the repository-wide verification successfully.

strategies: Avoid `path` as a variable name in zsh commands
Use descriptive loop variables such as `target_file`
Rerun interrupted verification from the beginning after correcting shell state
code_patterns: Avoid: for path in ...
Use: for target_file in ...

title: Residue scan treated audit history as active configuration
description: The Docker residue check excluded change logs and the changelog but still scanned the mistake knowledge base, which intentionally preserved removed filenames as verification context.
error_message: unexpected active Docker references: ./.agents/knowledge/mistakes-testing.json
root_cause: The scan did not distinguish active project configuration and documentation from immutable operational audit artifacts.
solution: Excluded `.agents/knowledge/**` alongside logs and the historical changelog, then reran the active-reference scan.

strategies: Define residue-scan scope before interpreting matches
Exclude audit and historical records that intentionally preserve removed terms
Report active and historical matches separately when both matter
code_patterns: Avoid: treating every repository match as active configuration
Use: explicit globs for active source and documentation scope

title: Combined development launcher ran without a port preflight
description: The smoke-test launcher attempted to start a second Yjs server on port 1234 even though a user-owned project server was already listening there.
error_message: Error: listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use ::1:1234
root_cause: The combined launcher was executed before checking whether its two local service ports were available.
solution: Inspected the listener without terminating it, confirmed it was an existing project Yjs process, and ran only the Next.js service for the HTTP smoke test.

strategies: Check expected development ports before starting combined process groups
Do not terminate existing listeners until their ownership and purpose are confirmed
code_patterns: Avoid: starting a second server blindly
Use: lsof -nP -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN before a smoke-test launcher

title: Active-reference scan did not exclude installed dependencies
description: The final stale-reference scan searched the workspace without explicitly excluding node_modules, and this non-git workspace did not apply .gitignore filtering as expected.
error_message: Matches for DATABASE_URL were reported from Next.js package documentation under node_modules.
root_cause: The scan relied on implicit ignore behavior even though the workspace is not a Git repository.
solution: Added an explicit --glob '!node_modules/**' exclusion and reran the active-source scan.

strategies: Explicitly exclude dependency and build directories in repository residue checks
Do not assume .gitignore filtering is active outside a Git worktree
code_patterns: Avoid: rg pattern . with implicit exclusions
Use: rg pattern --glob '!node_modules/**' --glob '!.next/**' .

title: Shared Next type artifacts conflicted across verification processes
description: The original verification batch started tsc and next build together, so Next.js regenerated .next/types while tsc was resolving it. The issue recurred when a user-owned dev server and prior production builds left duplicate generated files with a ` 2.ts` suffix, causing duplicate declarations during the requested acceptance retry.

context.code_snippet: Promise.all([npm run typecheck, npm run build])

error_message: TS6200 and TS2300: duplicate declarations from .next/types/cache-life.d 2.ts and routes.d 2.ts; original occurrence reported TS6053 missing generated files.
root_cause: Next development, production build, and standalone typecheck share the generated .next directory; overlapping or duplicated artifacts are not a safe typecheck input.
solution: Kept the user-owned dev process running, moved only the exact duplicate-suffixed generated files to a recoverable temporary folder, and reran verification sequentially.

strategies: Run next build and standalone tsc sequentially
Inspect .next/types for duplicate-suffixed artifacts when a dev process remains active
Only parallelize checks that do not mutate shared generated directories
code_patterns: Avoid: Promise.all([typecheck, next build])
Use: npm run build && npm run typecheck

title: Alternate-port Next dev smoke test still hit the project lock
description: A second next dev process was started on an alternate free port after port preflight showed 3000 occupied, but Next.js locks the project development directory rather than only its TCP port. The same mistake recurred during conflict-review acceptance on port 3002.
error_message: Another next dev server is already running (most recent PID 19264).
root_cause: The preflight checked port availability but not the per-project Next development lock.
solution: Left the user's active dev process untouched and used the completed production build with next start on an alternate port.

strategies: Check both listening ports and .next/dev lock state
Use next start for an isolated smoke test after a successful build
code_patterns: Avoid: assuming an alternate port permits a second next dev for one worktree
Use: npm run build followed by PORT=<free> npm start

title: Proxy assertion inspected the legacy middleware manifest
description: The first post-build proxy assertion checked middleware-manifest.json, which remains empty for this Next.js 16 Node proxy even though the build registered it.
error_message: Error: Proxy manifest is empty.
root_cause: The assertion targeted an older manifest shape instead of Next.js 16 functions-config-manifest.json.
solution: Verified /_middleware in functions-config-manifest.json and confirmed behavior with an actual unauthenticated HTTP 307 response.

strategies: Prefer an HTTP behavior assertion over internal artifact assumptions
For Next.js 16 Node proxy metadata, inspect functions-config-manifest.json
code_patterns: Avoid: requiring middleware entries from middleware-manifest.json
Use: functions['/_middleware'] plus an HTTP redirect smoke test
tests_to_add: Assert unauthenticated room requests return 307 and a /login Location

title: RLS-denied update was mistaken for a successful write
description: The viewer test treated a null PostgREST error as proof that UPDATE changed a row, but an RLS USING filter can produce a successful zero-row update.
error_message: Error: A viewer modified the shared document.
root_cause: The test asserted transport success/failure instead of database row effects.
solution: Added .select('id') to the update and now fails only when returned affected rows are non-empty.

strategies: For RLS-filtered UPDATE/DELETE tests, assert affected-row count or re-read the value
Distinguish PostgREST policy errors from silent zero-row filtering
code_patterns: Avoid: !error as proof an RLS mutation occurred
Use: mutation.select(primaryKey) and assert data.length

title: HTTP smoke required an exact Cache-Control string
description: The token-endpoint smoke compared Cache-Control to exactly 'private, no-store', but the request proxy intentionally added stronger compatible directives.
error_message: Error: Anonymous token response was not private 401.
root_cause: The test treated a set-like HTTP directive field as an ordered exact string.
solution: Parsed comma-separated directives and required both private and no-store while allowing stronger additions and arbitrary ordering.

strategies: Assert required Cache-Control directives semantically
Allow security-strengthening directives added by request middleware
code_patterns: Avoid: exact Cache-Control string equality
Use: normalized directive membership checks

title: Backticks in a double-quoted residue pattern triggered shell substitution
description: A final rg pattern included Markdown backticks inside a double-quoted shell command, so zsh attempted command substitution. The same unsafe nesting pattern later over-escaped a quoted status value in a Node plan-validator one-liner and produced invalid JavaScript.
error_message: zsh: command not found: DATABASE_URL
root_cause: Shell command substitution rules were overlooked while embedding Markdown punctuation in a double-quoted command argument.
solution: Reran the read-only scan with the entire regular expression single-quoted and no interpolated shell content.

strategies: Use single quotes for literal rg patterns containing backticks or dollar signs
Avoid Markdown formatting characters in shell patterns when plain text is sufficient
code_patterns: Avoid: rg "`literal`"
Use: rg 'literal'

title: Stale Next development cache referenced the old root proxy
description: The browser verification server reused generated Turbopack artifacts from before proxy.ts moved into src, so the login page opened a runtime error overlay instead of the current application.

context.code_snippet: Could not parse module '[project]/proxy.ts', file not found

error_message: Runtime Error: Could not parse module '[project]/proxy.ts', file not found.
root_cause: The generated .next development cache retained a reference to the former root-level proxy after the source file moved to src/proxy.ts.
solution: Stopped the test server, moved the exact .next directory to a recoverable temporary path, and restarted Next so it could discover src/proxy.ts from clean generated state.

strategies: Invalidate generated Next artifacts after moving proxy or middleware entry points
Run a real browser overlay check after structural framework file moves
code_patterns: Avoid: reusing .next after moving proxy.ts between framework discovery roots
Use: stop server, recoverably move .next, then restart
tests_to_add: Keep the browser error-overlay check in feature verification

title: Generated cache cleanup used a rejected permanent-delete command
description: The first attempt to invalidate the stale .next cache used rm -rf against an exact generated directory, which the command safety layer rejected.
error_message: rm -f style commands are not permitted. Use a safer approach.
root_cause: The cleanup chose permanent deletion even though a recoverable move was sufficient to invalidate the cache.
solution: Validated an explicit unused temporary target and moved .next there, preserving the generated artifact for recovery.

strategies: Prefer recoverable moves for generated cache invalidation
Resolve and validate both source and destination paths before moving a cache
code_patterns: Avoid: rm -rf project/.next
Use: mv project/.next /tmp/project-next-cache-stale-<timestamp>

title: Dependency source inspection guessed the wrong utils extension
description: A diagnostic command attempted to read node_modules/y-websocket/bin/utils.js, but this package version exposes the server utility implementation as utils.cjs.
error_message: IO error: node_modules/y-websocket/bin/utils.js: No such file or directory.
root_cause: The diagnostic assumed a JavaScript extension instead of resolving the installed package file list first.
solution: Listed the installed y-websocket files with rg --files, located utils.cjs, and inspected the correct source.

strategies: Resolve dependency source filenames with rg --files before opening guessed paths
Use the installed package layout as the source of truth
code_patterns: Avoid: assuming dependency source file extensions
Use: rg --files node_modules/package | rg pattern

title: Dynamic route path was not quoted in zsh
description: A source-inspection command passed src/app/rooms/[roomId]/actions.ts to zsh without quoting it, so zsh interpreted the brackets as a filename pattern and rejected the command before sed could read the file.
error_message: zsh: no matches found: src/app/rooms/[roomId]/actions.ts
root_cause: The diagnostic command did not quote a Next.js dynamic-route path containing shell glob metacharacters.
solution: Reran the inspection with the complete path enclosed in single quotes and read the server action successfully.

strategies: Quote every filesystem path containing brackets, spaces, parentheses, or wildcard characters
Treat Next.js dynamic-route paths as shell-sensitive by default
code_patterns: Avoid: sed ... src/app/rooms/[roomId]/actions.ts
Use: sed ... 'src/app/rooms/[roomId]/actions.ts'

title: Knowledge index lookup guessed the wrong filename
description: A diagnostic searched .agents/knowledge/index.json even though this repository stores its aggregate mistake metadata in mistakes-index.json.
error_message: rg: .agents/knowledge/index.json: No such file or directory
root_cause: The command assumed a generic index filename instead of resolving the repository's knowledge files first.
solution: Listed .agents/knowledge with rg --files, found mistakes-index.json, and inspected the correct file.

strategies: Resolve unfamiliar repository paths with rg --files before opening them
Reuse the exact filenames declared by project-specific skills
code_patterns: Avoid: guessing .agents knowledge filenames
Use: rg --files .agents/knowledge before inspection

title: Browser skill command was unavailable on PATH
description: The browser acceptance workflow invoked the agent-browser command documented by the installed Vercel skill, but this environment contains only the skill instructions and no executable on PATH. Earlier Chrome-control fallbacks reported no browser; the later password-reset session resolved the available in-app Browser plugin and completed visual acceptance there.
error_message: zsh: command not found: agent-browser; browser runtime: No browser is available
root_cause: The verification assumed the skill's companion CLI or a browser-control backend was available without first resolving either capability in the current environment.
solution: Confirmed the optional CLI is absent, then resolved the installed in-app Browser plugin, selected the available Chrome instance by URL, and completed desktop, mobile, redirect, and console acceptance with that supported fallback.

strategies: Run command -v before relying on an optional skill companion executable
Resolve the installed in-app Browser plugin before concluding that no browser runtime is available
Do not claim visual acceptance when both the CLI and runtime backend are absent
code_patterns: Avoid: invoking optional browser CLIs without a preflight
Use: command -v agent-browser and verify agent.browsers.list before planning visual acceptance

title: Focused SQL assertion reused the DO block dollar delimiter
description: The first post-migration assertion wrapped a PostgreSQL DO block in `$$` and also used `$$` for string literals inside that block, so the parser closed the block at the first inner literal.
error_message: ERROR: syntax error at or near 20260717045518
root_cause: The generated verification SQL used the same anonymous dollar-quote delimiter for nested lexical scopes.
solution: Changed the outer anonymous block to a distinct `$verify$` delimiter while preserving inner dollar-quoted literals, then reran the assertions.

strategies: Use named dollar tags for DO blocks that contain dollar-quoted literals
Keep verification SQL syntactically isolated from shell quoting
code_patterns: Avoid: DO $$ with inner $$string$$ values
Use: DO $verify$ with inner $$string$$ values
tests_to_add: Run the corrected remote room lifecycle assertion

title: Authenticated public-room join workflow failed integration verification
description: The first disposable room-management run passed schema assertions and public discovery but failed when an outsider attempted the explicit editor-membership insert for a public room.
error_message: new row violates row-level security policy for table room_members
root_cause: The legacy direct self-insert join policy rejected the Data API insert even after the room became publicly visible; room lifecycle mutations were split between hardened RPCs and a fragile table insert path.
solution: Added a dedicated authenticated `join_public_room(uuid)` security-definer function, revoked direct authenticated membership inserts, removed the obsolete join policy/helper, routed application and verification joins through the function, and passed the disposable public join/leave workflow.

strategies: Include the sanitized PostgREST error in authorization-test failures
Verify both policy predicates and returned affected rows
code_patterns: Avoid: authorization verifier errors that omit the database reason
Use: error.message or serialized returned rows without credentials
tests_to_add: Rerun the disposable public join and leave workflow after diagnosis

title: Offline-sync fixture still used revoked direct room insertion
description: The first collaboration regression run passed Yjs and version-history checks, then the offline-sync fixture failed before its behavior test because it still created rooms, memberships, and documents with direct table inserts.
error_message: Could not create the offline verification room.
root_cause: The dependency audit updated the version-history fixture but missed the second authenticated test fixture that depended on the now-revoked partial room insert path.
solution: Migrated the offline fixture to `create_study_room`, consumed its generated slug/id, and selected the atomically provisioned notes document.

strategies: Search every test and script for writes to a table before revoking a direct mutation privilege
Keep all authenticated room fixtures on the production atomic creation boundary
code_patterns: Avoid: test-only sequential rooms/room_members/documents inserts
Use: create_study_room RPC and assert its invariants

title: Inline Node database check lost nested SQL quotes
description: A final read-only migration and residue check embedded JavaScript and SQL single-quoted literals inside a shell single-quoted `node -e` program. The shell stripped the inner SQL quotes and PostgreSQL rejected the diagnostic before executing any query.
error_message: ERROR: syntax error at or near comma
root_cause: The diagnostic crossed shell, JavaScript, and SQL quoting layers without isolating the SQL source, so nested single quotes were consumed by the shell.
solution: Use the existing environment-aware schema verifier pattern with SQL passed through a shell-safe JavaScript source form, then rerun the read-only consistency query.

strategies: Avoid nesting same-delimiter SQL strings inside shell-quoted inline programs
Prefer a checked script or an argument form that keeps SQL out of shell lexical parsing
code_patterns: Avoid: shell single quote -> node -e -> SQL single quotes
Use: shell-safe double-quoted JavaScript program with an escaped SQL template literal
tests_to_add: Rerun the migration history and disposable-fixture residue query

title: Knowledge validation assumed a nonexistent index wrapper
description: A final metadata assertion tried to read statistics.by_category even though this repository stores total_mistakes and categories at the root of mistakes-index.json.
error_message: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'by_category')
root_cause: The verification command assumed a generic metadata schema instead of inspecting the repository's existing index structure before asserting its totals.
solution: Read the index first, then validate Object.values(index.categories) against index.total_mistakes.

strategies: Inspect repository-owned JSON schemas before writing ad hoc assertions
Validate the fields that are present rather than assuming a conventional wrapper
code_patterns: Avoid: index.statistics.by_category
Use: Object.values(index.categories) and index.total_mistakes

title: Dev smoke command assigned zsh's read-only status variable
description: The final HTTP smoke command stored curl's response code in `status`, which is a read-only special parameter in zsh, so the shell stopped before checking the response body.
error_message: zsh: read-only variable: status
root_cause: The verification command used a common shell variable name without accounting for zsh's reserved special parameters.
solution: Renamed the variable to the task-specific `rooms_http_code` and reran the HTTP response and error-marker checks.

strategies: Use task-specific variable names in zsh verification commands
Avoid special parameters such as status, path, and pipestatus
code_patterns: Avoid: status=$(curl ...)
Use: rooms_http_code=$(curl ...)

title: Chrome controller rejected its documented network-idle wait state
description: The Phase 4 browser acceptance opened the local login URL successfully, then the connected Chrome controller rejected `networkidle` even though its emitted API reference listed that load state.
error_message: playwright_wait_for_load_state does not support networkidle
root_cause: The browser controller's runtime capability is narrower than the load-state union exposed in its generated documentation.
solution: Kept the successfully opened tab, switched to the supported `domcontentloaded` state, and verified meaningful DOM content directly.

strategies: Use DOM-ready plus targeted element/state assertions with this Chrome controller
Treat network-idle as optional unless the active browser backend confirms support
code_patterns: Avoid: assuming every documented load state is implemented by each browser backend
Use: domcontentloaded followed by a targeted DOM snapshot or element wait

title: Dense inline browser metric expression had one extra parenthesis
description: The first mobile target-size measurement packed an awaited browser evaluation, nested object literal, and output call onto one expression and failed to parse before reading the page.
error_message: Unexpected token: ')'
root_cause: A dense inline expression made the nested evaluation and output-call delimiters difficult to audit.
solution: Separated the evaluation result into a named binding with a block-bodied callback, then emitted the completed metrics object; the corrected check confirmed zero overflow and accessible target sizes.

strategies: Use named intermediate results for nontrivial browser evaluations
Prefer multiline block-bodied callbacks when returning nested metric objects
code_patterns: Avoid: deeply nested await/evaluate/write calls on one line
Use: const metrics = await evaluate(() => { return {...}; }); write(metrics)
